Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City 22 20?!} www.dilq.qov.ph 2024 DILG NO C$ MARIA REMEDIOS CHUA-SY, DMD jhingsy@yahoo.com Dear Maam Chua-Sy: This has reference to your electronic mail dated 29 January 2024 seeking the Department's legal opinion on whether the Certificate to File Action issued by the Lupon Tagapamayapa is only meant to be filed in Courts alone. Per the representation, over the course of 3 years, you have filed several barangay cases against a neighbor regarding their continuous harassment and unjust vexation because of your complaint against their trucks which uses your street as their terminal reducing a 2-way lane into a I-way street. You represented that these trucks are a consequence of their commercial business whose business permit and license to operate was eventually revoked by BPLO Caloocan because of non-issuance of a Zoning Clearance. Our subdivision, BF Homes Ph I and 2 is an R2 Zone. You then stated that the issue is that the Lupon Tagapamayapa of Barangay 169 has continually insists that the CFA is for filing in the courts only despite having shown to them that the CFA indicates that it can be filed "in court/government agency". You mentioned that the "confusion" stems from the fact that the heading of a CFA states "Certificate to File COURT Action"; and yet the contents indicate also the words "/government agency". Thus, the request for legal opinion. At the onset, it is imperative to discuss what a Certificate to File Action is. A Certificate to File Action is a document issued by the Lupon Tagapamayapa or Pangkat Tagapagsundo secretary indicating that the dispute could not be settled amicably at the barangay level, allowing the parties involved to pursue legal action in higher courts if they wish. It essentially certifies that the parties have undergone the Barangay justice process but were unable to reach a resolution. The issuance of a certification to file action means that the complainant may already bring his case to the court or other government office for adjudication. In connection with this, Administrative Circular No. 14-93 dated July 15, 1993 specifically provides: "II. Under the provisions of R.A. 7160 on Katarungang Pambarangay conciliation, as implemented by the Katarungang Pambarangay Rules and Regulations promulgated by the Secretary of Justice, the certification for filing a complaint in court or any government office shall be issued by 1 Alinsungay V. Judge Cagampang Jr., G.R. No. 1--69334 July 28, 1986 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Barangay authorities only upon compliance with the following requirements: 1. Issued by the Lupon Secretary and attested by the Lupon Chairman (Punong Barangay), certifying that a confrontation of the parties has taken place and that a conciliation settlement has been reached, but the same has been subsequently repudiated (Sec. 412, Revised Katarungang Pambarangay Law; Sec. 2[h], Rule Ill, Katarungang Pambarangay Rules); 2. Issued by the Pangkat Secretary and attested by the Pangkat Chairman, certifying that: a. a confrontation of the parties took place but no conciliation/settlement has been reached (Sec. 4[fl, Rule III, Katarungang Pambarangay Rules; or b. that no personal confrontation took place before the Pangkat through no fault of the complainant (Sec. 4[fl, Rule III, Katarungang Pambarangay Rules). 3. Issued by the Punong Barangay, as requested by the proper party on the ground of failure of settlement where the dispute involves members of the same indigenous cultural community, which shall be settled in accordance with the customs and traditions of that particular cultural community, or where one or more of the parties to the aforesaid dispute belong to the minority and the parties mutually agreed to submit their dispute to the indigenous system of amicable settlement, and there has been no settlement as certified by the datu or tribal leader or elder to the Punong Barangay of place of settlement (Secs. 1,4 & 5, Rule IX, Katarungang Pambarangay Rules); and xxxx" From the foregoing, it is evident that the Certificate to File Action granted by the Lupon Tagapamayapa or Pangkat Tagapag%ndo secretary can also be filed in other government offices for adjudication if the requirements outlined above are met. Thus, the Certificate to File Action is not limited to filing a complaint in court. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, AU ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY AN VICTOR R. LLAMAS secretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs O LLAJJVRULLLS-LRALLDnas Page 2 of 2
